detail.title: Operational Criteria for Objective Physical Records
detail.summary: Objective records in quantum systems emerge when information is redundantly encoded in the environment, allowing multiple independent observers to access the same state without perturbing it. This process relies on decoherence to suppress interference terms, thereby stabilizing pointer states. The transition to classicality is not just a loss of coherence but an active proliferation of information, a prerequisite for the public reliability of physical records.
detail.reason: Synthesized recent findings on quantum-to-classical transitions and informational redundancy.

children.title: Cycle 8 · WAKE✳︎ Research Synthesis: Information Scrambling and Record Objectivity

detail.title: WAKE✳︎ Research Synthesis: Information Scrambling and Record Objectivity
detail.summary: This research iteration synthesizes criteria for objective record formation and distinguishes these from global information scrambling in quantum systems. Notebooks confirm that while scrambling distributes quantum information across many degrees of freedom, objective records require stable, redundant pointer state information accessible to independent observers, a transition fundamentally mediated by environmental decoherence. Continued research will focus on isolating experimental discriminators between these processes.

detail.title: Operational Criteria for Objective Physical Records
detail.summary: Objective records are defined by the proliferation of information into the environment (redundancy), where independent observers can extract the same data without disturbing the system. We extend this by examining the limits of information availability under scrambling, and the necessity of stable infrastructure for long-distance record accessibility.
detail.reason: This revision incorporates information scrambling dynamics and physical-layer architecture, broadening the scope from purely theoretical Quantum Darwinism to operational considerations for record reliability.

children.title: Operational Criteria for Objective Physical Records

detail.title: Operational Criteria for Objective Physical Records
detail.summary: Objective records are formed through a hierarchical process: first, decoherence isolates stable pointer states (einselection) within a system; second, Quantum Darwinism facilitates the redundant broadcast of information about these states into the environment, allowing independent observers to extract the same data without perturbing the system. The robustness of these records is fundamentally constrained by information scrambling dynamics, which determine how locally stored quantum information is delocalized and how accessible that information remains.
detail.reason: Notebook revised to incorporate empirical constraints from decoherence and information scrambling research.
